key_insight: A hierarchy of ideal-hydrodynamic models describes tornado formation as rotating convection driven by thermal instability, with coordinated growth of velocity components.
engineering_relevance: The models offer a theoretical framework for investigating vortex initiation, near-surface inflow, and peak wind locations in tornado-like flows.
method: Link convective onset to the Schwarzschild instability criterion.
Develop simplest, refined, and full models coupling stream function, azimuthal velocity, and density change at increasing levels of complexity.
Construct an analytical solution for the simplest model and examine single-whirlwind and two-eyed tornado configurations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical modeling and predicted flow structures, but provides no quantitative validation against observations or experiments.
watch_item: Ideal-hydrodynamic assumptions and boundary-condition-sensitive rotation may limit applicability to real atmospheric tornadoes.
paper_title: Some generalizations of the tornado model
